info.title: The Argus local API
info.summary: 55 endpoints for profiles, proxies, cookies, automations and schedules, 53 of them fronted by MCP tools.
info.description:
This is a local API. It listens on loopback on the machine running Argus, and nothing off that machine can reach it. There is no hosted web API.

The server starts with the Argus launcher and stops with it. Keys are created in the launcher under the API tab, may be scoped to folders, and the first call from a new client raises an approve-or-deny prompt that holds the request until it is answered.

Generated from the launcher's own route table. The human version of this document is https://www.browserargus.com/api-reference, and the same content as Markdown is https://www.browserargus.com/api-reference.md.

servers.description: Loopback on the machine running Argus. There is no hosted equivalent of this URL.

tags.name: Profiles
tags.description: A profile is an isolated browser identity with its own proxy, fingerprint and cookie jar. You can read them, change them, and open one for automation — but you cannot mint one from here. Creating an identity is done in the app, because a script that makes fifty of them makes fifty that look alike.

tags.name: Proxies
tags.description: The proxy library, and the check that tells you whether an entry still works. Listing proxies never returns their credentials: the response is read by a model as often as by your code.

tags.name: Cookies
tags.description: Bulk cookie import, for moving a jar you already have into a profile. Both routes are HTTP-only — no agent tool fronts them.

tags.name: Monitoring
tags.description: Report the outcome of a run back to the launcher, with an optional screenshot, so a sweep across many profiles has somewhere to land.

tags.name: Automations
tags.description: Author and run automations. Creating, changing and deleting one needs a key with no folder scope, because automations are shared across every folder and have none of their own. A folder-scoped key may still list, read and run them.

tags.name: Schedule
tags.description: A schedule entry is an ordered list of automations with a time on it — a different thing from the schedule an automation carries itself, which runs that one automation alone. Entries fire only while the launcher is open: a time it was closed for is recorded as missed and skipped, never caught up. Occurrences is the record of what ran, not the plan for what will.

tags.name: Tables
tags.description: Read and set which columns the launcher's own tables show. The one part of the API that changes what you see rather than what runs.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: A skill is the working brief the in-app assistant loads for one job — instructions, worked examples, a reference shelf, and the pack of tools it may reach. Saving one creates a custom skill, or writes a local override of a built-in. Deleting is not the mirror image: a custom skill goes, while a built-in is reset to the brief it shipped with.

post.summary: Create a profile
post.description:
Create a profile

Create a browser profile. Only name is required; everything else gets the same defaults the app's own New Profile dialog uses -- status Ready, a random colour, a stable Windows 11 fingerprint, no proxy. proxyMode 'assigned' needs proxyId to name a proxy from the library (argus_list_proxies); omit both to create a direct-connection profile. Returns the created profile. Its id is permanent: it doubles as the on-disk browser-data directory name.

MCP tool: `argus_create_profile`.

post.summary: Read a profile's notes, newest first
post.description:
Read a profile's notes, newest first

The notes on a profile, newest first -- what it is for, who it belongs to, what has been tried on it. Each note carries its author and when it was written. Read this before acting on an unfamiliar profile: it is where the humans running this workspace write down the things the profile's name and tags cannot say.

MCP tool: `argus_profile_notes`.

post.summary: Append a note to a profile
post.description:
Append a note to a profile

Append a note to a profile's thread -- what you did to it, what you found, why it is set up the way it is. The note is filed under this API key's own name and marked as written by an agent, so it is distinguishable from what a person wrote. Notes are append-only over the API: there is no tool to edit or delete one, including your own.

MCP tool: `argus_add_profile_note`.

post.summary: Move an automation to Trash. It stops running on launch and on its schedule
post.description:
Move an automation to Trash. It stops running on launch and on its schedule

Move an automation to Trash, where it stays for 30 days and can be restored from the app. It immediately stops running on launch and on any schedule, and disappears from argus_list_automations. Profiles keep it attached so that a restore puts them back as they were. Past runs stay readable. There is no API to restore or to delete permanently: both are done in the app.

MCP tool: `argus_delete_automation`.

Needs a key with no folder scope; a folder-scoped key is refused with 403.

post.summary: Create a scheduled workflow
post.description:
Create a scheduled workflow

Schedule automations to run one after another at a set time. `recurrence` is {kind, at, date?, days?, from?, until?, tz?}: kind is 'once' (with date 'YYYY-MM-DD'), 'daily', or 'weekly' (with days, 0=Sunday..6=Saturday); at is 'HH:MM' 24-hour; tz is an optional IANA zone like 'Europe/Berlin', and without it the time is read on whatever machine runs it. `from` and `until` bound a daily or weekly schedule to a date range, both 'YYYY-MM-DD' and both inclusive -- WITHOUT `until` a repeat runs forever, so set it whenever the request names a period ('next week', 'until the 30th'); a 'once' takes neither, since it already names its day. `steps` is an ordered list of {automationId, profileIds, stopOnFail}: each step runs its automation on each profile in turn, the next step starts when the last finishes, and an empty profileIds means a browserless run. Get ids from argus_list_automations and argus_list_profiles. Entries fire only while the Argus launcher is open; a time it was closed for is skipped, never caught up.

MCP tool: `argus_create_schedule_entry`.

Needs a key with no folder scope; a folder-scoped key is refused with 403.

get.summary: The vocabulary a skill is written in: tool packs, entry tabs, shelf ids
get.description:
The vocabulary a skill is written in: tool packs, entry tabs, shelf ids

The vocabulary an assistant skill is written in. Call this before argus_save_skill rather than guessing: it returns the tool PACK names a skill may claim (with the tools in each), the tab ids that may be claimed as entry tabs and who holds each one, every knowledge-base article id available for the reference shelf, and the field limits. Every tab is held by a built-in and a custom skill outranks one, so `claimedBy` is context rather than a blocklist -- only a tab held by another CUSTOM skill is refused. The same role argus_automation_schema plays for steps.

MCP tool: `argus_skills_schema`.

post.summary: Create a custom skill, or edit a built-in one
post.description:
Create a custom skill, or edit a built-in one

Create or edit an assistant skill. Omit skillId to create (the id is slugged from the title and returned); title and instructions are required then. Pass a built-in's id to edit it -- that writes a local override, and only title, blurb, instructions, examples and docs apply; sending toolPack or entryTabs for a built-in is refused, because those are code-defined. EVERY FIELD YOU SEND REPLACES THAT FIELD and fields you omit are left as they are, so call argus_get_skill first and send only what changes; an empty examples array deletes them. toolPack must be one of the packs argus_skills_schema lists; it is the ONLY way a skill gets tools, and naming tools directly is not possible by design. Unknown doc ids and already-claimed tabs are dropped and reported back in `dropped` rather than failing the call. THIS CALL BLOCKS: it raises an approve-or-deny card in the app naming your key, and returns 403 if the user denies or lets it lapse.

MCP tool: `argus_save_skill`.

Skills are one document per workspace and apply to every folder's assistant, so a folder scope has nothing to narrow here. Use an unscoped key to author one.

This call blocks while an approve-or-deny card is shown in the launcher, and answers 403 if it is denied or allowed to lapse.

skillId.description: Omit to create a custom skill. A built-in's id edits that built-in.

title.description: Required when CREATING; omit it when editing and the current title is kept. Up to 60 characters.

blurb.description: One line, up to 200 characters. The ONLY part always in the assistant's context -- it is what the model reads to decide the skill applies, so write it as a routing decision, not a summary.

instructions.description: The working brief. Required when CREATING; omit it when editing and the current brief is kept. Never hand-write a reference shelf or an example list into it -- both are appended from the fields below.

examples.description: Two to four verbatim requests in the user's voice, one line each, up to 120 characters.

toolPack.description: A pack name from argus_skills_schema. Absent means documentation and navigation only. Custom skills only.

entryTabs.description: Tab ids this skill is suggested on, taking the tab from whichever built-in covers it. Only a tab another CUSTOM skill already holds is dropped. Custom skills only.

docs.description: Knowledge-base article ids for the reference shelf, e.g. concepts/proxies. Ids the KB does not have are dropped.

hidden.description: Built-ins only: true removes the skill from the assistant entirely. Undo it with argus_delete_skill on the same id.

post.summary: Delete a custom skill, or reset a built-in to its shipped brief
post.description:
Delete a custom skill, or reset a built-in to its shipped brief

On a CUSTOM skill id this removes the skill. On a BUILT-IN id it does not remove anything -- it clears the local override and restores the shipped brief, which is also how a hidden built-in comes back. That asymmetry is deliberate: built-ins ship with the app and cannot be deleted, only edited or hidden. The user must approve this in the app.

MCP tool: `argus_delete_skill`.

Skills are one document per workspace and apply to every folder's assistant, so a folder scope has nothing to narrow here. Use an unscoped key to author one.

This call blocks while an approve-or-deny card is shown in the launcher, and answers 403 if it is denied or allowed to lapse.
